groups.title: Flightless birds
groups.explanation: None of these birds can fly, and the ostrich is the largest bird alive.

groups.title: Moons of Saturn
groups.explanation: Each of these moons circles Saturn, and Titan is larger than Mercury.

groups.title: Constellations
groups.explanation: All four are constellations of the northern winter and summer skies.

sources.excerpt: The largest (both heaviest and tallest) flightless bird, which is also the largest living bird in general, is the common ostrich (2.7 m, 156 kg).
There are over 60 extant species, including the well-known ratites (ostriches (Struthio), emus (Dromaius), cassowaries (Casuarius), rheas, kiwis (Apteryx)), and penguins (Sphenisciformes).
Saturn's moons are diverse in size, ranging from tiny moonlets to Titan, which is larger than the planet Mercury and the second largest moon in the Solar System.
Four orbit inside of the diffuse G ring or between the major moons Mimas and Enceladus.

Twenty-five of the confirmed moons are regular satellites; they have prograde orbits not greatly inclined to Saturn's equatorial plane (except Iapetus, which has a prograde but significantly inclined orbit).
Later, the Cassini spacecraft made multiple flybys of Dione throughout the 2000s and 2010s as part of its campaign to explore the Saturn system.
Orion is most prominent during winter evenings in the Northern Hemisphere, as are five other constellations that have stars in the Winter Hexagon asterism.
Beginning at the north, Lyra is bordered by Draco, Hercules, Vulpecula, and Cygnus.
